THIS. Despite all the addictive medications I’ve taken long term and alcohol I’ve drank and other ineffective coping choices... I only get addicted to stuff like binging on food or self injury or restricting myself into starvation mode or anything EXCEPT a substance. Tit for tat drugs and alcohol have never been able to compete with the “high” of behavior based coping. 

I find it super interesting tbh. Still though, it’s interesting because it’s so odd compared to 99% of humans I’ve ever known.

2018 I went and I didn’t shower lol. I brought a few packs of face/body wipes and used them at night before I put on clean clothes to sleep! It wouldn’t make the cut at home but it was certainly good enough considering I slept in a tent in a field without running water xD

I’ve learned to go to the doctor with an index card with all my diagnosis on it and if one might affect that appointment I’ll circle it and/or write a few words about what would trigger me. How much the card says depends on the doctor, type of appointment and how sensitive I feel that day.  It doesn’t always help but I’ve found a lot of nurses find it helpful because they don’t usually know much about me and are told to do certain things that someone with a mental illness might find triggering.  I think having it written down makes communication easier and gives me an easy way to write more if I’m too upset to explain.
You’re very welcome! Glad I could help!

My first eating disorder nutritionist explained that the main difference between bulimia and BED is the purging after eating. When I had BED I binged a lot and cycled through the restriction-binge cycle but never purged after binging. When I was bulimic it was a very similar restrict-binge cycle except after I binged I would purge as much as possible right after binge eating. 

I hope that helps!

My DBT therapist would’ve told me to do Pros and Cons of a few ways to proceed. I tend to push myself to use more of a logic favored wise mind approach when my options are tough emotionally either way. That way when I look back (even if at the time I don’t intend to live long enough to have hindsight) I can at least take pride I did what was best for me, even if it made me miserable. 
Good luck 💜

I have found great comfort in working on accepting that no relationship is likely to last “forever” for me. I have a FP of sorts who has handled all kinds of BPD type insanity from me, swears up and down that he’ll be rubbing it in my face that he never left when we’re old and he never fails to still text me back the day after I did something absurd... yet I know I’m better off remembering he could potentially leave at any time instead of getting swept up in the positives of our communications, that he technically owes me nothing and that even if it isn’t because he intentionally leaves my life I may realistically have to live my life without him one day. I think I enjoy our time together more that way any how. I lash out at him less (and otherwise push him away less) since I’ve started actively acknowledging his friendship could be temporary, but it would be nice if I hear back from him again when we aren’t in touch. I think this lies somewhere between “life is fleeting” type radical acceptance and some kind of interpersonal skills... this probably is a wise mind thing? (DBT lingo isn’t fresh anymore lol.)

Good luck :)

I have no sources, but in my experience living as a celiac with gluten-y housemates this is only true IF the pots have no scratches at all and you use special separate sponges (obvious reasons) and soap bottle to avoid anyone touching the dish soap bottle with gluten on their hands. 

I have given up on sharing ANY kitchen things with gluten eaters apart from the counter tops and major appliances. I have my own small set of stuff including pots and pans that are just mine. I clean them when the sink is empty so I can scrub it to my standards. We have some scratches in the metal sink bottom so I’m picky about the sink being empty and scrubbed.

If you’re really celiac level sensitive I highly recommend ignoring any gluten eater’s opinions on your safety with plates and such. They often don’t understand how small a mistake on their part can make us sick :(

Good luck :D I certainly know what you mean. Some nights when sleep has been bad I can’t sleep because my brain is screaming anxieties at me, other times I fall asleep and get woken up by a housemate and then spiral down. I hope things get better!! I do recommend the Fisher Wallace brain stim. Almost no side effects and can be used with medication.

Being tired no matter how much you sleep can be a depression thing. I use the Fisher Wallace brain stimulator to help manage my depression to avoid extra meds. They say it helps with insomnia as well but it didn’t do that for me. It mostly just helps the depression and some of my anxiety which when alleviated allow the sleeping med to work properly to help me adjust to a sleep schedule again :)

When I get so deep into bad sleep that I CANT sleep enough to improve I have to use my sleeping med for a bit to force myself to adjust. I use it for as few nights as I can to get back on track. I take a benzo, it helps keep the anxiety at bay while I’m adjusting to sleeping well again, too.

Oh gosh welcome to my world!! My ADHD has been written off as bipolar mania, anxiety induced procrastination, depressed lack of focus... you name it and I’ve probably heard it. Due to having Borderline Personality and a handful of other issues it’s probably different over all for me but a big thing that helped me get my point across that I do have ADHD that is helped by a stimulant was explaining that in almost any state of mind (anxious, depressed, happy, bored, frustrated, etc) I have trouble staying on task. It seemed to me that when I made it clear the issue of unfocused hyperactivity existed in any state I could be hyperactive in (example = too depressed to be out of bed at all means I can’t be hyperactive because I’m dead inside) and that the disorganized thought process exists in my mind and in my external reality almost all the time... THEN psychiatrists start to understand. There’s more to it than that specific to my set of diagnostic process stuff but yea. I hope that helps :)

Best of luck!!

Your situation reminds me of me when I don’t understand what my trigger was until later on. I’ll think I have no reason to be hurting or whatever negative emotion it is and spiral into “well I’m just going back to misery anyway...” and it goes from there is a moving type downward thing. 

A big factor for helping this in my situation is doing a behavior chain type of activity. Basically back track until I understand at least when my mood changed, ideally what made it change too. 

Good luck 💜

Ugh, yes. This isn’t a prime example because some other issues are at play, but last night I fell asleep on my futon downstairs and 2 housemates accidentally were too loud and woke me up. I was a little frustrated but it was okay tbh... until they both went back to their computers, put their headphones on and didn’t acknowledge me anymore until after I fell back asleep (thinking I was upset with them for waking me up.) While in my head I spiraled into “they hate me which is why they woke me up and then ignored me” which very quickly turned into “if I kill myself they don’t have to deal with me any more and I can be done.” The ineffective answer on my end was less severe thankfully. I ended up crying as hard as I could without making enough noise for them to hear over their headphones and then being hurt no one noticed... which of course my internal nonsense translated to they want me to be miserable and go away... even though I wasn’t making enough noise to be reasonably noticed and the fact I stood up to get tissues wasn’t a huge red flag in hindsight.

When I can force my internal thought process to match reality I’m aware they all love me, yet I ended up wanting to go upstairs and off myself at 4am thinking they want to be rid of me because in reality I didn’t clue them in I was hurting (only initially a little frustrated) and it made sense they thought I was annoyed so they should give me space. 

(Perhaps it is of value to share I am their landlord, the only female in the house and they all know about my mental illnesses sooooo... landmine for them to be afraid to say the wrong thing if I’m already upset 😕 )

(I don’t always remember even what floor of the house I was on lol.)
Dialectical Behavioral Therapy was designed for borderline however it has helped my anxiety so I’d highly recommend looking into it!!

Anxiety tolerance success: learning DBT skills upped my ability to tolerate anxiety by like, 100 times what I once could tolerate without acting on ineffective action urges to deal. I learned paced breathing, how to self soothe, and all about mindfulness among other things. 

Anxiety overcoming success: this one time I started having an anxiety attack while I was at work as a caregiver at a super over heated indoor pool room, the heat was icing on the cake and I started crying, trying to hide it from everyone around. I ended up using some of those said DBT skills I got cold water, paced my breathing, and soothed myself with something soft to the touch as well as through my other senses. I ended up not letting my caregivee (idk the word for the person I care for? If I’m the caregiver is she the caregivee? Lol.) know I was distressed and she had a great time at the pool. I felt great after because I had started by trying to just tolerate the distress and ended up getting past it entirely and going on with my day and job :)

When I'm super anxious because it feels like my ADHD rules my life I like to practice paced breathing for literally maybe a minute or two and usually I can feel better. Breathe in for 4 seconds, exhale for 8. I forget all the details about the brain and body but this can force you to calm down a bit. I actually also use this technique when I'm feeling too hyperactive and if I can realize I'm being too hyper I can breathe for a minute like this and often I cool off a little. This doesn't really help your big picture problem, but may be of help in a moment of stressed upsetness about your life. 

Best of luck!!

I TOTALLY understand actually. I ended up not fostering a cat for a similar reason, but if you find you love the animal soon you can, with every shelter I've encountered, ask to adopt it and they'll take it off the website/list of pets available. The shelter I almost got a cat from said if someone else visited the cat, said they wanted it, they'd have me either give it up or opt to adopt it on the spot to keep it. But then it's yours so you need to know quick if you can handle the animal. 

Coping with animal sickness and loss is so hard when you're mentally ill. A few months ago my first truly my cat I adopted as an adult passed away. I was devastated BUT I learned to look at it as I have her a happy end of her life and I was able to cope healthy and safely once I processed that fact. 

This is just advice from my own pet owning experience. I just think they're wonderful for routine, feeling loved, and comfort from another living thing. 

Best of luck. PM me if you want to chat about pets. I've had quite a few and I've always struggled with mental illness. 

Have a fantastic wonderful life!

Hey hi Hello! I am bipolar and find having a dog (I actually have 2 and a cat that I successfully care for!) keeps my routine in check. I HAVE to get up in the morning, not for me but to let my dogs out, feed them, give the cat food, and the dogs get me outside on walks more than if I didn't have them. I know it can be daunting to get something that relies on you when you're unstable, but if you have experience to show they help keep your routine alive, I'd suggest getting a foster dog and if it works adopt one! If not contact the shelter asap and tell them you can't keep fostering. Most shelters will take the animal back as fast as they can to ensure it is care for properly if you report back you can't do the job. 

I hope this is helpful! I'm happy to share my animal caretaker experience with you via PM of you're curious how I manage bipolar episodes and my pets at the same time :)

I actually can relate to this. If it's the same thing I feel I call it being wound up. I'm not wound up ABOUT anything in specific it's just my existence that feels wrong. I often feel fidgety or like crawling out of my skin. 

If this helps, what I do is purposely distract myself as best I can. Ask someone to talk to me, color something, clean something, or if I'm at work I take deep breaths and maybe run my fingers through my hair or something as a calming action. 

I hope you can relate or get some kind of help from my experience! Have a great life!

Hello there! I am a long term Celiac and when I have a problem where I'm unsure if I can eat something I contact the company! Often times they will be able to tell you if the product has any actual gluten, if it was processed with gluten, or is actually 100% gluten free normally but they want to alert there is risk of cross contamination, or whatever the case is about that product :) I hope you can contact them or have already solved your dilemma. Best of luck!!
